body.cap: A humanoid equipped with Tommoro Robotics’ Robot Foundation Model performing logistics picking tasks at the CES 2026 HUMANOID M.AX Alliance pavilion. | Photo by AVING News

body.x: Tommoro Robotics (CEO Byoung-Tak Zhang) participated on January 6 (local time) in the HUMANOID M.AX Alliance pavilion at CES 2026, where visitors could view a consolidated showcase of “Korean-style humanoid” technologies.

Tommoro Robotics is an AI-focused robotics startup and a core participant in the government-led K-Humanoid Alliance. Building on advanced research accumulated at Seoul National University’s Biointelligence Lab prior to its spin-off, the company provides general-purpose humanoid intelligence applicable across logistics, manufacturing, retail, and food and beverage environments.

A key strength of Tommoro Robotics lies in its comprehensive technology stack encompassing Robot Foundation Models (RFM) and robot AI solutions, forming an end-to-end (E2E) Physical AI platform. The platform is designed to combine real-time data acquisition, automated AI model learning, and ultra-fast on-device computation. In practice, this enables robots to perceive their surroundings and objects in real time, reason about the situation, and immediately execute actions suited to the outcome.

At CES 2026, a humanoid powered by Tommoro Robotics’ autonomous AI control platform demonstrated coordinated collaboration in a logistics scenario, drawing strong interest from attendees. Driven by an RFM, the robot precisely assessed rapidly changing environments and unstructured objects, generating optimal actions for each situation.

body.cap: Tommoro Robotics is demonstrating a robot hand at the CES 2026 HUMANOID M.AX Alliance pavilion. | Photo by AVING News

body.x: In particular, the robot performed tasks at speeds and with consistency that met real industrial requirements, earning positive reactions. Observers noted that the demonstration effectively addressed technical barriers that have hindered the commercialization of enterprise-grade humanoids, while also highlighting strong potential for expansion into broader manufacturing and service applications.

Looking ahead, Tommoro Robotics plans to use CES 2026 as a springboard to globalize its Physical AI platform and broaden its industrial footprint. A company representative said, “Through prior automation proof-of-concept projects with multiple domestic logistics companies, we have validated real-world applicability. Based on this, we aim to expand partnerships for verification and localization across additional industries.”

The representative added, “In particular, we plan to enter the U.S. market, which is the world’s largest robotics market and the most advanced in understanding Physical AI and humanoid platforms, to take the lead in standardizing RFM technologies. At the same time, we will build on the references accumulated in Korea to extend applications to markets beyond the U.S. and accelerate full-scale business expansion.”

The HUMANOID M.AX Alliance is a public-private consultative body formed in April 2025 with the participation of 260 organizations and companies, including AI research institutes, robot manufacturers, component suppliers, and universities and research institutions. The alliance jointly promotes the demonstration and commercialization of AI-based humanoids in industrial environments. At CES 2026, the HUMANOID M.AX Alliance Pavilion went beyond simple product displays and presented a practical model for ecosystem building by connecting AI, platform, and component technologies.
